entries.object: Results feed vs the official page: the one fixture recorded as pending
entries.observed: The official page prints 'Steelers 18, Bengals 38, FINAL, Sunday, November 15th'. The committed feed (data/results_feed.csv) carries row 2026_10_PIT_CIN with status in_progress and away_score 0 / home_score 0, with a note saying the scores are capture-time state and not a result. The Monday-night fixture 2026_10_LAC_BAL is labelled scheduled with blank scores; it was live (17-7, Q2) when checked.
entries.consequence: Replaying the feed's finals gives the official record for 29 of the 31 clubs whose record this session transcribed; the only two that fail are PIT and CIN, the two clubs in the one fixture the feed still holds open. Applying the published 18-38 reconciles 31 of 31. Two hazards follow: the corpus is a game short of what it claims, and a row with numeric 0-0 and a non-final status will poison any consumer that reads scores without reading status.
affects: every margin and total feature derived from the feed
entries.status_after_check: new finding - the feed needs a rebuild from a fresh capture; the owning script is tools/build_results_feed.py, so the correction is requested in COORDINATION.md rather than hand-edited into another session's artefact

entries.object: Reproducibility of the committed pages under their own generators
entries.observed: Ran the repo's own generators (scripts/make_pages.py, scripts/build_site.py, tools/repo_audit.py) and diffed against the committed tree. docs/*.html changed in 11 files: the regenerated navigation drops the hand-added cross-link to ../hub/index.html ('Decision Hub') that is present in the committed pages. fl2-dashboard/data/repo-audit.json changed because it embeds the branch name and the HEAD commit of whoever ran it. The changes were reverted by this session; no other section's file is modified by this PR.
entries.consequence: Two committed artefacts cannot be regenerated without losing content that a later session added by hand, and one of them rewrites its own provenance on every run. The Pages 'validate' job runs make_pages.py and build_site.py but never diffs the result, so the drift is invisible in CI and will be silently destroyed the next time someone regenerates and commits.
affects: brief line: 'Add a drift alarm to every scraper'
entries.status_after_check: new finding - reported rather than fixed, because the fix touches other sections' files; board row DS-10 asks for the generator or the link to change, not both
entries.kind_note: not a league fact: this row records something observed inside the repository, so it cites the file it concerns rather than an official page
